title: BSCAveraging
abstract:
Three theorems about binary channels on a doubly symmetric binary source: a pair (𝑋, 𝑌) of
Bernoulli(1/2) bits with P(𝑋 ≠ 𝑌) = 𝑝, together with Markov chains 𝑈 - 𝑋 - 𝑌 - 𝑉 in which 𝑈
and 𝑉 are the outputs of two independent binary channels applied to 𝑋 and to 𝑌. Let 𝒜 be the
set of rate triples (𝑅₀, 𝑅₁, 𝑅₂) with 𝐼(𝑈;𝑋) ≤ 𝑅₁, 𝐼(𝑌;𝑉) ≤ 𝑅₂ and 𝑅₀ ≤ 𝐼(𝑈;𝑉) attainable by
arbitrary binary channels on the two sides, and ℬ the same set with both channels restricted
to be binary symmetric.

(1) conv 𝒜 = conv ℬ for every 𝑝 in [0,1]. (2) At 𝑝 = 0, no pair of binary channels whose rates
do not exceed those of the Z-channel with parameter 𝑎 and the S-channel with parameter 𝑑
attains a larger 𝐼(𝑈;𝑉) than that pair does. (3) At 𝑝 = 0, no pair of binary channels whose
rates are at least those of the Z-channels with parameters 𝑎 and 𝑑 attains a smaller 𝐼(𝑈;𝑉)
than that pair does. Here 𝑎, 𝑑 range over (0,1).
